title: Mixlen flow smoother and KV reserve tuner for continuous scheduler
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response lengths cause slot churn in the continuous scheduler and unpredictable KV cache residency, increasing GPU memory fragmentation and tail latency. Observed 95th token latencies spike during multi-turn flows with alternating short/long turns.

Goal: Create a tuner that smooths mixlen flow (reduce destructive slot preemption) while adaptively reserving KV residency for in-flight dialogues, reducing eviction churn and improving p95/p99 latencies without regressing throughput or cost efficiency.

This ticket scopes a prototype tuner + experiments, instrumentation changes to trace per-dialogue KV residency, and a phased rollout plan to validate on canary capacity before platform-wide rollout.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token latency for mixed-turn workloads reduced by >= 15% on canary compared to baseline
KV eviction rate per-GPU decreased by >= 20% during mixed-length trace replay
No throughput loss (>1%) on steady-state long-only and short-only synthetic workloads
Telemetry added: per-dialogue KV residency histogram and slot-preempt events exported to console
Canary rollout plan and automated rollback on latency/cost regressions defined
technical_details:
Design summary: introduce a MixLen Flow Smoother (MLFS) layer in the continuous scheduler that maintains a small temporal cohorting window (configurable ms horizon) and bias slot allocation to favor short-turn coalescing when it reduces churn. Pair MLFS with a KV Reserve Tuner (KVR) that computes per-shard soft-reserve quotas derived from recent dialogue 'hotness' (turn frequency * average token length) and enforces low-cost pinning for top-N hot dialogues.

Key knobs:
- smoothing_horizon_ms (default 120ms)
- cohort_weight (0.0-1.0) controlling trade-off between immediate packing and cohort retention
- kvr_decay_tau (seconds) for hotness half-life
- kvr_soft_reserve_ratio (fraction of GPU KV memory to treat as soft-reserved)

Runtime changes: actor scheduler updates to track per-dialogue metrics, lightweight bloom-style hotness estimator to avoid large per-dialogue state, and eviction policy augmentation to prefer evicting low-hotness, low-recently-accessed slots. Quantization/packing strategy unchanged.

Implementation constraints: avoid linear increase in per-dialogue state; all estimators must be O(1) amortized and vectorizable for GPU-host co-design.
experiment_plan: Phase A (lab): implement MLFS + KVR in dev branch, unit tests for estimator correctness and invariants

Phase B (bench): run mixed-turn replay traces (internal chatbot + customer anonymized trace) on single-node perf cluster, collect p50/p95/p99 token latency, batch coalescing efficiency, KV eviction rate, and memory fragmentation metrics

Phase C (canary): deploy to 5% of traffic in staging cluster configured with runtime-1.20 canary pool; run controlled load generator to exercise 60/40 mix of skewed-turn and symmetric-turn flows for 48h

Phase D (metrics sweep): full telemetry sweep, analyze cost delta (tokens/$) and perform rollback criteria checks; iterate knob tuning (smoothing_horizon_ms, kvr_soft_reserve_ratio) based on sweep results
Phase E (gradual rollout): 20% -> 50% -> 100% rollout only if canary meets acceptance criteria
metrics: batch_coalesce_ratio (percentage of slots coalesced per epoch)
comments: Asha Patel (2025-02-10): Created ticket. Initial hypothesis comes from multiple SLO incidents where alternating short/long turns caused repeated KV evictions. Refer to incident notes 2025-01-29 in postmortem.
Marco Liu (2025-02-11): Spike branch created. Implemented a compact hotness estimator using 64-bit counters per-shard + LRU sampling. Pushed initial microbench.

Jonas Berg (2025-02-13): Review: concern about smoothing_horizon_ms default of 200ms; suggests starting lower (80-120ms) to avoid harming latency-sensitive paths. Also asked for safety net to disable MLFS for routes tagged 'low-latency'.
Marco Liu (2025-02-14): Updated knobs: smoothing_horizon_ms default 120ms, added route opt-out label. Added unit tests for hotness decay correctness.

Priya Desai (2025-02-17): Bench results attached: mixed-turn replay across 3 runs shows p95 reduction avg 18%, KV eviction rate down 27%, negligible throughput change. Observed slight p50 regression (2%) on short-only workload when smoothing_horizon_ms > 200ms.

SRE Team (2025-02-19): Canary run checklist created. Need auto-rollback hook if p99 token latency increases by >10% or KV eviction reduces latency but increases cold-start errors in downstream tracing (observed in earlier experiments).
Marco Liu (2025-02-22): Deployed canary to staging 5% traffic. Early telemetry: p95 down 16%, kv_eviction_count down 22%, gpu_memory_frag_ratio improved by 6 points. Monitoring for regressions.

Asha Patel (2025-02-25): Interim decision: proceed with 20% rollout after additional 24h of stable canary. Documented knob defaults and rollback criteria in confluence. Next: bake user-level QA (sampled customer chat flows) and schedule post-rollout review in Cycle 43.
notes: Risk: Over-reserving KV for 'hot' dialogues could starve bulk inference jobs; mitigated by soft-reserve and autoshrink under pressure.
Trade-off: Cohorting improves p95 for mixed workloads but can harm p50 for purely short prompt traffic; we will gate via per-route labels and gradual rollout.
Decision log: Use exponential decay hotness with tau=60s initially; iterate based on canary telemetry.
